title: Support Operations Report: Cost, Speed, Reopening and Satisfaction
executive_summary: Analysis of 347 cleaned support tickets joined to the agent roster shows total labor cost of $27,422.90 and a mean resolution time of 75.2 minutes. Team Beta carries the highest labor cost, chat is the slowest channel, and email tickets reopen at 17.24% — a 119.83% relative increase over chat's 7.84%. Only 12 tickets combine high cost with low satisfaction, and workload is spread across 18 agents with the busiest handling just 7.49% of volume.

key_findings.statement: The export contains 347 tickets with a mean resolution time of 75.2 minutes and a total labor cost of $27,422.90, equivalent to roughly $79.03 per ticket.
Team Beta generated the highest total labor cost at $10,247.36, followed by Gamma at $9,387.73 and Alpha at $7,787.81; Beta's total exceeds Alpha's by $2,459.55.
Chat is the slowest channel with a mean resolution time of 83.0 minutes, ahead of email (73.0 minutes) and phone (69.3 minutes); chat takes about 13.79 minutes longer than phone on average.
Email tickets reopen at 17.24% versus 7.84% for chat — 9.4 percentage points higher, a relative increase of 119.83% for email over chat.
12 tickets (3.46% of all tickets) combine high labor cost (>= $100) with a low satisfaction score (<= 2); this segment's reopen rate is 8.33%.

Resolution time is right-skewed: the median is 65 minutes, below the 75.2-minute mean, with a standard deviation of 51.9 minutes. Mean satisfaction is 4.15, and 19 tickets (5.48%) are missing a satisfaction score.

18 unique agents handled the tickets. The busiest agent handled 26 tickets, a 7.49% share of total volume, compared with an average of about 19.28 tickets per agent, indicating no extreme concentration.

limitations: 19 tickets (about 5.5%) lack satisfaction scores; if missingness is not random, satisfaction-based findings may be biased.
All comparisons are descriptive, not causal: ticket complexity, priority, customer type and agent tenure were not controlled for.
The export covers a single period with no time dimension, so trends over time cannot be assessed.
The high-cost/low-satisfaction thresholds ($100, <=2) are arbitrary cutoffs, and the resulting segment of 12 tickets is too small for strong statistical inference.
Agent concentration is summarized only by the top agent's share; a full workload distribution (e.g., Gini coefficient) was not computed.
conclusion: Support operations are broadly healthy: satisfaction averages 4.15 and workload is evenly spread across 18 agents. Priorities are (1) investigating why email tickets reopen at 17.24% — more than double chat's rate — and (2) reviewing chat handling, the slowest channel at 83.0 minutes on average. The 12 high-cost, low-satisfaction tickets warrant individual follow-up, and satisfaction capture should be improved to close the 5.5% data gap.
